note: He clears the commercial half comfortably — owns a property management business running a few hundred doors plus a development arm, and has previously carried $1,500 a month in personal training, so both occupation and capacity to pay are there. He fails the other three, and fails the exclusion by name. At 6'0" and 265 lb against an athletic baseline of 195-205, he is roughly 65 lb heavy, which is past the 'not like we have dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight' line the ICP is quoted as drawing. His health is not the neglected area, it is the presenting problem: two bulging lumbar discs, bilateral shoulder impingement, stretched knee ligaments, chronic inflammation and pain getting out of bed. And his own framing is rescue rather than optimisation — 'pain-free' as the biggest goal, 65 lb to lose, a first child arriving. The one criterion he does not fail is gym-aversion; he completed 75 Hard and misses training. This is the clearest 'outside the stated ICP' case in the batch on the stated criteria, and note that the criterion that should have caught him first — whether the body can safely do loaded kettlebell work — still does not exist in the ICP at all.
